doc_name: List of Walt Disney anthology television series episodes (seasons 1–29)
text: The original incarnation of the anthology series was created to fund the development and construction of Disneyland, with the television program initially focusing on and showcasing the park's original four lands.[1][2][3] The show was hosted by Jiminy Cricket.[13] It was nominated for an Emmy Award for Best New Television Personality for Walt Disney.[6][7] and won an Emmy Award for Best Show of the Year.[6][10] Available on the DVD Walt Disney Treasures: Disneyland USA, the series featured cartoons such as Reason and Emotion, Chicken Little, and How to Have an Accident in the Home.[42] It was also known as Ducking Disaster with Donald and His Friends.[43] The program reused footage from Man in Space, Man and the Moon, and Mars and Beyond, and included excerpts from Beezy Bear, How to Sleep, Aquamania, In the Bag, and The Litterbug.[47] These segments were later aired and released on home video as Goofing Around with Donald Duck. The series was directed by Hamilton Luske, and one episode included sequences from Melody Time, Make Mine Music, and the deleted "Clair de Lune" sequence from Fantasia; when rerun in 1970, the "Clair de Lune" sequence was replaced with scenes from Sleeping Beauty, which was then undergoing a theatrical reissue. At the start of the 5th season, ABC rebranded the show as Walt Disney Presents, and it was moved from ABC to NBC to enable color broadcasting. At the start of the 16th season, NBC rebranded the show as The Wonderful World of Disney. During a special episode, the shorts The Cold-Blooded Penguin (from The Three Caballeros) and Goliath II were featured. Ron Howard and Suzanne Somers served as hosts for the special, with the second night being a 2-hour presentation that included a complete showing of Dumbo, plus highlights from Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs, Pinocchio, and Cinderella. At the start of the 26th season, NBC rebranded the show as Disney's Wonderful World. Note: All of the following episodes were first aired on CBS.
